name: Himsa
label: Revelation
lede: Seattle hardcore kids flipped a word for nonviolence into a band name, played through a dozen members, said no to a lot of tours, and quit right after what was reportedly their best record. Eight years on, they came back on Halloween.

eras.title: Ahimsa, minus the A
eras.text: Hardcore had spent a decade preaching ahimsa, the Krishna-conscious principle of nonviolence. A crew of Seattle scene lifers flipped it to himsa, harm, and pointed the band at Swedish-style metal instead of Youth Crew. Revelation, the label that had put out Shelter, signed them.

years.h: Five Seattle hardcore kids start Himsa
years.p: Singer Christian "Xtian" Schmitt, guitarist Brian Johnson, bassist [[Derek Harn|882786bf-e5af-441b-b416-e46bc7ac5e1a]] and drummer Mike Green start the band, with guitarists Henry and Aaron Edge in the first lineup.
years.xp: The name is the Sanskrit word for harm or violence, the inverse of ahimsa, the nonviolence principle that straight edge's Krishna wing had been preaching for years. Himsa took the opposite word and kept the hardcore address book.

years.h: A self-titled 7" lands on Revelation
years.p: Himsa's first record is a self-titled EP on Revelation. The first press includes 220 on blue vinyl.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ground Breaking Ceremony · Revelation Records: pressing history
years.h: Ground Breaking Ceremony, the album with the first singer
years.p: Cut at Raimstorm Studio with Steve Carter and Paul Speer producing. It's the only Himsa full-length without John Pettibone.
years.xp: Christian Schmitt sings. The album opens on a short instrumental and then leans long: several songs run past four minutes. The first press included 223 on clear vinyl.

eras.title: The singer from Undertow
eras.text: Within a year of Himsa's debut the band had burned through singers, drummers and a keyboard player. What came out the other side was John Pettibone, voice of the Seattle straight edge band Undertow, and the lineup that made Himsa's name.

years.src: No Echo: John Pettibone interview · Wikipedia: Himsa
years.h: Undertow's John Pettibone takes the mic
years.p: After Christian Schmitt leaves and Chris LaPointe passes through, [[John Pettibone|eea60dae-22af-4e2c-89d3-ff675e97f548]] becomes Himsa's singer. [[Kirby Charles Johnson|a2e52b31-705d-4ef4-9d68-83d2b15517c6]] joins on guitar and Tim Mullen settles in on drums.
years.xp:
Pettibone had known the founders since the early '90s Seattle hardcore scene; half of them, he told No Echo, had been in Trial. He was moving back from New York in January 2000 and Himsa needed a vocalist.

The switch to Swedish-leaning metal was easy, he said: "I was still just growling into a microphone." The 2000 turnover also brought and lost drummer John Harnett, guitarist EJ Bastien and keyboardist Clay Layton.

years.src: Revelation Records: pressing history · Wikipedia: Himsa
years.h: Pettibone's first Himsa record is their last for Revelation
years.p: Death Is Infinite is the first Himsa album with John Pettibone singing. The first press was 300 on green vinyl and 820 on black.

eras.title: Lamb of God makes a phone call
eras.text: Himsa landed on Prosthetic, a label barely off the ground, and grew up with it. They also earned a reputation as the band that said no to tours and festivals, because the D.I.Y. rules they'd learned in hardcore still applied.

q: We were stern to the D.I.Y. ethic
years.h: Lamb of God introduces Himsa to Prosthetic
years.p: John Pettibone says [[Lamb of God|298909e4-ebcb-47b8-95e9-cc53b087fc65]] saw Himsa at a local show, liked what they heard and connected them with Prosthetic Records.
years.xp:
Prosthetic was in its early days, and Himsa grew with it. The friction came later. Himsa turned down tours and festivals the label wanted, and label support faded.

Pettibone's explanation: "We were stern to the D.I.Y. ethic from our background in the hardcore scene, and that doesn't sit well with a larger label."

years.h: Two Seattle-area studios for the next album
years.p: Himsa record Courting Tragedy and Disaster at Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline, Washington, and Orbit Audio in Seattle, with Steve Carter producing.

yt: Rain to the Sound of Panic, music video
years.h: Courting Tragedy and Disaster arrives on Prosthetic
years.p: Brandan Schieppati of [[Bleeding Through|55fd865d-4a0d-4fd0-af19-7e6feb168ab8]] and original guitarist Aaron Edge add backing vocals over Swedish-style twin guitar leads and hardcore screaming.
years.xp: The lineup: John Pettibone, Kirby Charles Johnson, Sammi Curr on guitar and keys, Derek Harn and Tim Mullen. Critics lumped it in with [[Darkest Hour|e0ededb4-6085-4f68-90f7-89bc560930a3]], [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] and God Forbid.
play: Rain to the Sound of Panic

years.h: Chad Davis takes over the drum kit from Tim Mullen
years.p: Mullen leaves after Courting Tragedy and Disaster and Davis steps in. Guitarist Matt Wicklund joins the same year and stays until 2005.

yt: Rain to the Sound of Panic, NEMHF 2003
years.h: Himsa play Rain to the Sound of Panic at New England Metal and Hardcore Fest
years.p: Footage from the 2003 festival set, the single from Courting Tragedy and Disaster.

yt: You've Seen Too Much, full live DVD
years.h: Himsa put a tour on DVD
years.p: You've Seen Too Much collects live and tour footage.

years.h: Himsa fly to Denmark for Hail Horror
years.p: For their third album they leave the Northwest and record in Denmark, a short hop from the Swedish metal they'd been chasing since 1998.

eras.title: A lineup that holds, then the end
eras.text: The band finally stopped changing members, signed to Century Media and toured three continents. Then, with Summon in Thunder just out, Himsa called it.

yt: Hail Horror record release show, Seattle, 2006
years.h: Hail Horror is Himsa's last album for Prosthetic
years.p: The Denmark sessions come out as Himsa's third full-length.

years.h: A package tour with Darkest Hour and the Acacia Strain
years.p: Himsa hit the road with [[Darkest Hour|e0ededb4-6085-4f68-90f7-89bc560930a3]], [[The Acacia Strain|08bebce9-33fa-4ae9-9992-4e5d137d655b]], A Life Once Lost and Dead to Fall.

years.h: Australia with Parkway Drive, then a Century Media deal
years.p: Himsa tour Australia with [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]] and Cry Murder, and sign with Century Media Records the same month.

years.h: Chad Davis leaves; Joe Frothingham takes the drums
years.p: Frothingham plays drums for the band's final year.

years.cap: Himsa outside Hell's Kitchen, Tacoma, July 2007
years.h: Summon in Thunder, produced vocals and all
years.p: Sessions begin April 23, 2007, at Robert Lang and Woodshed, with [[Devin Townsend|93e8c41e-8e4f-4d08-bbf5-bc1a903b2423]] producing the vocals. Videos follow for Unleash Carnage and Big Timber.
years.xp: It's Himsa's only album for Century Media and, reportedly, the best of the four.

years.big: It's time to let it go.
years.src: Lambgoat: Himsa calls it quits · Last.fm
years.h: Derek Harn announces the end of Himsa
years.p: The bassist says the band is ending after ten-plus years and four releases, even though everyone is getting along and Summon in Thunder is reportedly their best.
years.xp:
Harn's statement was nearly cheerful: "We've got a great label. We're getting along, we've toured and we're fine. It's all good." The last three years, he wrote, had been relatively stable after almost incomprehensible, constant upheaval.

Last.fm's summary puts it down to touring burnout, with John Pettibone moving to side projects and done with long tours.

years.h: Last show, El Corazon, Seattle
years.p: Himsa play their final show at El Corazon, the Seattle club once called the Off Ramp. John Pettibone would later run production there.

years.src: Wikipedia: John Pettibone · No Echo: John Pettibone interview
years.h: Pettibone's next band is Heiress
years.p: Four months after the last Himsa show, John Pettibone fronts the Seattle band Heiress.
years.xp: He'd already sung in The Vows and Iamthethorn. After Himsa he also tour-managed [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and sang backup on their 2009 album Axe to Fall.

eras.title: Rehearsing as Crushpile
eras.text: Himsa came back quietly and on home ground: warm-up shows under fake names, then Halloween at the club where they'd quit.

yt: Secret show at Slim's Last Chance, July 16, 2016
years.h: Crushpile and Metalmucul play the warm-ups
years.p: Himsa test the waters with practice shows under those two names before admitting who they are.

years.cap: Himsa at the Highline Bar, Seattle, 2018
yt: A Girl In Glass, El Corazon, 2016
years.h: Himsa come home to El Corazon on Halloween
years.p: John Pettibone, Derek Harn, Kirby Charles Johnson, Sammi Curr and Chad Davis play El Corazon eight years after the last show there. Reunion shows stay in the Seattle area.

years.cap: Himsa at Northwest Terror Fest, Highline Bar, Seattle, June 2, 2018
years.h: Northwest Terror Fest books Himsa
years.p: Himsa play Seattle's Northwest Terror Fest, one of the rare dates of the reunion.
